title: Projectile

slow_motion.evidence: No narration, captions, or on-screen text indicate slow motion.

subjects.description: small blue spherical ball moving across the grid

observation.what_happens: A small blue ball travels from the upper left toward the lower right across a tiled wall. It is already in flight at the start of the clip and is still falling toward the brown floor at the end.

calibration.note: scale from the fall itself: 4666 px/s² over 7 arcs = g of 9.807 m/s²

given: g = 9.807 m/s² (Earth); it set the scale, so treat g as known and fixed
reasoning: x moves steadily forward while y falls and rises repeatedly to near -0.94 m, so this is ballistic flight interrupted by floor bounces. Bounce height shrinks slowly, requiring gravity plus restitution, with air on Earth motivating no-drag vs linear vs quadratic drag and friction variants.

critique.why_it_won: It nails the arc and bounce without any air drag, which the drag model only confirms by fading to nothing.

headline: Blue ball arcs, bounces, and keeps falling freely.
finding: It falls freely under gravity 9.81 m/s² and hits the floor at -0.95 ± 7.75e-4 m, bouncing back with springiness 0.88 ± 2.29e-4.

eyeball.law_in_words: projectile motion under uniform gravity with constant horizontal velocity and vertical velocity reversing at the floor scaled by the normal restitution
